methyldiazinol.summary: A 1965 laboratory DHT-derived steroid with a high reported animal muscle-to-androgen ratio, the basis of its interest for building muscle.

quick.overview:
Methyldiazinol is an oral steroid made in the 1960s as a modified version of mestanolone. The appearance payoff people associate with it is more muscle mass.

It is a 17α-methylated DHT analogue, so it is presumed to work by activating the androgen receptor. An old animal measurement reported a muscle-to-androgenic ratio of 15 relative to oral methyltestosterone, among the highest in the early literature. It was never marketed, and no human studies have been published.
quick.how: There is no established practical use. It was never sold as a drug, and it appears only in the 1965 chemistry paper and in later descriptions of that work, so there is no routine, form or timeline to describe.
quick.risks: No human safety data exist and it has no approved use. As a 17α-methylated oral androgen, it belongs to a class associated with liver strain and androgenic side effects, but its own effects in people have not been described.

angle.text: The interest in methyldiazinol is muscle gain: it is a DHT-type steroid that reportedly activated androgen receptors strongly relative to its androgenic effect in animals. That 1965 animal measurement is the whole basis for the idea, and it was never marketed or tested in people.

epistane-epitiostanol-derivative-havoc.summary: An oral designer steroid sold as a supplement since about 2009 for a harder, leaner muscular look; case reports link it to liver bile-flow problems.

quick.overview:
Epistane (also Havoc or Epi Plex) is an oral anabolic steroid derived from epitiostanol, a Japanese breast-cancer drug. Lifters use it for muscle gain with less water retention, which they associate with a harder, leaner look.

It is a 17α-methylated androgen from the DHT family, and lab work on human liver cells suggests it raises bile acid synthesis and interacts with nuclear receptors. It appeared in online muscle supplements around 2009. No clinical trials have tested it for muscle or appearance; the literature is chemical analysis of products and a small set of case reports.
quick.how: It has been sold as an oral over-the-counter-style supplement, typically in capsule form, and used in bodybuilding contexts for a drier, harder look rather than bulk. People using it have commonly paired it with liver-support products, though this has not been studied for it.
quick.risks: A 2020 case series described four users with prolonged cholestasis, and its 17α-methyl group is associated with liver toxicity. It has been a controlled steroid in the US since 2014 under the Designer Anabolic Steroid Control Act and is prohibited by WADA.

angle.text: Epistane is used by lifters who want muscle gain with less water, giving a harder, leaner look. It is an androgen-receptor-activating DHT-family steroid sold as a supplement since about 2009; no trials exist, and case reports link it to prolonged cholestasis.

methoxydienone-methoxy-18-methyl.summary: A nandrolone-family steroid from contraceptive research that turned up as a designer muscle supplement; no human trials exist.

quick.overview:
Methoxydienone (Methoxy, 18-methyl) is a 19-nortestosterone steroid synthesised in the 1960s and 70s during progestin research. It later showed up in online supplements sold for muscle building.

It is an anabolic-androgenic steroid and progestogen, and animal-derived ratios reported on Wikipedia suggest anabolic activity when injected. Oral activity in humans has not been characterised, and no clinical studies have examined it in people.
quick.how: It has been sold as an oral designer supplement ingredient for muscle gain. Beyond that, there is no documented routine, and no data on how quickly results appear.
quick.risks: No human safety data are published. A 2022 case report tied a supplement containing it to a detected 18-methyl steroid metabolite in a forensic urine sample, which matters for drug testing in sport.

angle.text: Methoxydienone is sold as a designer supplement for muscle gain, based on its nandrolone-like steroid structure and the idea that it activates androgen receptors to build muscle. It comes from 1960s contraceptive research, and the human literature on it is a forensic case report.

bolandione.summary: A nandrolone prohormone sold over the counter in the US until 2005 for muscle gain; now controlled and known for causing doping-test positives.

quick.overview:
Bolandione (19-norandrostenedione) is a prohormone the body converts to nandrolone, and it was sold as a muscle supplement in the US until 2005. The payoff people wanted was more muscle mass.

Oral intake leads to conversion to nandrolone, while its own androgen receptor activity is weaker than DHT. Animal data suggest oral routes are inefficient for muscle, per Wikipedia. It is mostly remembered for doping research: trace amounts in androstenedione products produced false-positive nandrolone tests in the early 2000s.
quick.how: In the supplement era it was taken orally as a over-the-counter prohormone product by bodybuilders. It is no longer sold legally in the US.
quick.risks: It is a US Schedule III controlled substance and banned under the World Anti-Doping Code. Animal data suggest oral use may cause side effects even where muscle effects are inefficient.

angle.text: Bolandione was used as a prohormone: the body converts it to nandrolone, which activates androgen receptors and supports muscle gain. It was sold over the counter in the US until 2005; it is now controlled, and human evidence on physique effects is limited.

19-nor-4-androstenedione-19-norandrosten.summary: A nandrolone prohormone sold over the counter in the US until 2005 for muscle gain, now mostly a doping-control topic.

quick.overview:
19-Norandrostenedione is a prohormone that converts to nandrolone in the body. Bodybuilders used it in the US supplement era, until 2005, for more muscle mass.

After oral intake it converts to nandrolone and shares its urinary metabolite. The research on it centres on doping tests rather than muscle outcomes; a 2000 JAMA study looked at trace contamination of androstenedione products and whether ingestion causes positive tests for a nandrolone metabolite.
quick.how: It was taken orally as an over-the-counter supplement and stacked in bodybuilding routines. It is no longer legally sold in the US.
quick.risks: It is US Schedule III and prohibited in sport. Contaminated supplements have caused positive nandrolone tests.

angle.text: This prohormone converts to nandrolone, which activates androgen receptors and supports muscle growth. It was sold over the counter in the US until 2005 and used by bodybuilders; published work on it focuses on doping tests, not physique outcomes.

trendione.summary: A trenbolone metabolite sold online as a prohormone-type supplement for muscle and a harder look; studied mostly in cattle-manure research.

quick.overview:
Trendione (Trenavar) is a metabolite of trenbolone that has been sold online as a prohormone-type supplement. People use it for more muscle and a harder look.

It is inactive itself in receptor assays, with more than 100-fold lower affinity than trenbolone for androgen and progesterone receptors; the idea is that the body converts it to trenbolone. Most published work on it concerns environmental fate, since trenbolone acetate is used as a cattle growth implant and trendione is excreted in manure. No human studies exist.
quick.how: It has been sold as an oral supplement through online channels. No standard routine or timeline is documented.
quick.risks: No human safety data exist. It is listed in the US Designer Anabolic Steroid Control Act of 2014, so legal restrictions apply there.

angle.text: Trendione is sold as a trenbolone-type prohormone for more muscle and a harder look, on the idea that the body converts it to trenbolone and activates androgen receptors. It has been studied mostly in cattle-manure environmental work, not in people.

dienedione.summary: A trenbolone-type prohormone sold as a muscle supplement until it was scheduled in the US in 2010; no human studies exist.

quick.overview:
Dienedione is a 19-nortestosterone steroid sold as a bodybuilding prohormone, often marketed as a trenbolone prohormone, for more muscle mass.

It is thought to act as a prohormone to dienolone, which is structurally close to trenbolone and activates the androgen receptor. It became a US Schedule III steroid on January 4, 2010. Published research is limited to doping control, notably in horses, and no human studies exist.
quick.how: It was taken orally as a supplement in bodybuilding circles before scheduling. No documented routine or timeline exists.
quick.risks: No human safety data exist. It is controlled in the US (Schedule III) and UK (Class C) and prohibited in sport.

angle.text: Dienedione was marketed as a trenbolone-type prohormone for muscle gain: the body is thought to convert it to dienolone, which activates androgen receptors. It was sold until scheduled in 2010, and no human studies exist.

4-androstenediol-4-ad.summary: An early-2000s oral testosterone prohormone supplement marketed to raise testosterone and support muscle growth.

quick.overview:
4-Androstenediol (4-AD) is a steroid closely related to testosterone that was sold as an oral supplement in the 2000s. It was marketed to raise testosterone and build muscle.

It is described as converting to testosterone in the body at a low rate, and some of the resulting testosterone can convert to estrogen. Rat testis tissue can make the conversion in vitro, and the compound has been studied mainly for doping detection. A review of the wider prohormone class concluded that marketing claims for testosterone, strength and muscle gains had not been well supported by controlled human studies. No trial of it for physique goals was found.
quick.how: It was taken orally as a supplement in the early 2000s, typically as part of bodybuilding stacks of the prohormone era.
quick.risks: Reviews of oral andro prohormones raised health concerns, and related 19-nor prohormones are on the WADA prohibited list. Specific legal status was not documented.

angle.text: 4-AD was sold as a prohormone that converts to testosterone, raising androgen signalling to support more muscle. A review of the prohormone class found its marketing claims had not been well supported by controlled human studies.

1-androsterone-1-andro.summary: A designer DHEA-type prohormone sold online for muscle gain; documented mainly in seizure and doping-detection papers.

quick.overview:
1-Androsterone (1-Andro, 1-DHEA) is an oral designer steroid sold online as a dietary supplement for muscle gain. Chemically it is an isomer of DHEA.

It is described as a prohormone converted in the body to 1-testosterone and related androgens, which act on the androgen receptor. It appears in the literature mainly through a 2011 study of a product seized by German investigators, which characterised its urinary elimination for doping control. No human trials of its effects were found.
quick.how: It has been sold as an oral supplement, usually in capsule products marketed to lifters. No documented routine or timeline exists.
quick.risks: No human safety data exist. Authorities and anti-doping bodies treat such designer androgens as pharmacologically related to anabolic steroids.

angle.text: 1-Andro is sold as a prohormone that converts to 1-testosterone and related androgens, for more muscle mass. It is known from seizure and doping-detection papers, and no human trials exist.

adrenosterone-11-keto-androstenedione.summary: A natural adrenal steroid sold as '11-OXO' for fat loss and a leaner physique, via a proposed cortisol-blocking mechanism.

quick.overview:
Adrenosterone (11-keto-androstenedione, sold as 11-OXO) is a steroid made in the adrenal glands, sold since about 2007 as a supplement for fat loss and muscle gain. The look people want is leaner and more defined.

Proponents attribute the effect to inhibition of 11β-HSD1, the enzyme that converts cortisone to cortisol, which would reduce cortisol activity so less fat is stored and more lean mass is kept. It is also a precursor of 11-ketotestosterone, and its own androgen activity is extremely weak. No human trial of the supplement for body composition was found; published work covers doping detection and 11-oxygenated androgens in conditions such as PCOS.
quick.how: It is sold as an oral supplement, usually marketed alongside diet and training for body recomposition.
quick.risks: No supplement safety data from trials were found. Its legal status is not documented here, and anti-doping labs have developed ways to detect it.

angle.text: Adrenosterone is sold for fat loss and a leaner, more defined look, on the idea that it blocks cortisol production through 11β-HSD1 so less fat is stored. It is a natural adrenal steroid; the mechanism is a proposal, and supplement trials in people are lacking.

mebolazine-dymethazine.summary: A formerly prescribed oral steroid, a dimer of methasterone, that resurfaced in gray-market supplements for lean mass gains.

quick.overview:
Mebolazine (dimethazine) is an oral anabolic steroid once sold as a medicine (Dostalon, Roxilon) and later withdrawn. From about 2008 it reappeared in gray-market supplements marketed to bodybuilders for lean mass and a fuller physique.

It is a 17α-alkylated DHT derivative and an unusual dimer of methasterone, reportedly acting as a prodrug of methasterone, an androgen receptor agonist. No clinical trials were found; published research is limited to metabolism studies.
quick.how: It has appeared as an oral ingredient, sometimes unlisted, in supplement products used in bodybuilding.
quick.risks: The FDA has taken legal action against makers of supplements containing it, and it is classed with the hepatotoxic oral steroids. Human safety data are absent.

angle.text: Mebolazine is used for lean mass gains and a fuller physique: it is reportedly converted to methasterone, which activates androgen receptors and drives muscle protein gain. It turned up in gray-market supplements; no human studies exist.

mestanolone.summary: An old oral 17-methyl DHT steroid, strongly androgenic and weakly anabolic, discussed for strength and hardness; mostly discontinued.

quick.overview:
Mestanolone is a mid-20th-century oral steroid derived from DHT, marketed by about 1960 for example as sublingual tablets. Bodybuilders discuss it for strength and a hard look.

It activates the androgen receptor directly and cannot convert to estrogen; the 17-methyl group allows oral activity. It was later found to be mainly androgenic with weak anabolic effects. It remains available in Japan but is mostly discontinued elsewhere, and the literature is mostly doping analysis; it is also a metabolite of oxymetholone.
quick.how: It was used orally or sublingually as a medicine. Current use in physique circles is based on discussion rather than documented routines.
quick.risks: Reported effects include virilisation and liver damage, as with other 17α-alkylated steroids. It is Schedule III in the US and controlled in many other countries.

angle.text: Mestanolone is an oral DHT-type androgen discussed for strength and a harder look, since it activates androgen receptors directly without converting to estrogen. It was found to be mostly androgenic with weak anabolic effects, and modern trials are absent.

stenbolone.summary: A DHT-derived anabolic steroid related to drostanolone, discussed for lean muscle and a harder look; known from metabolism studies.

quick.overview:
Stenbolone is a DHT-derived anabolic steroid related to drostanolone and 1-testosterone. It is mentioned in bodybuilding circles for lean muscle and a drier, harder look.

It acts as an androgen receptor agonist. Only its 17β-acetate ester was sold, as a depot intramuscular injection under names such as Anatrofin and Stenobolone. Human data are limited to metabolism: after a single oral dose of the acetate to a volunteer, researchers identified nine urinary metabolites and detected the parent compound for more than 120 hours.
quick.how: Its acetate ester was historically a depot injectable. Current physique use is based on discussion rather than documented routines.
quick.risks: No clinical safety data were found beyond its classification as an anabolic steroid. Legal status was not documented in the sources reviewed.

angle.text: Stenbolone is discussed for lean muscle and a drier, harder look, since it is a DHT-derived steroid that activates androgen receptors. It is known mostly from metabolism and doping-detection studies.

mepitiostane-thioderon.summary: Japanese oral prodrug of the antiestrogen steroid epitiostanol, discussed for a drier, leaner look; sold as a breast-cancer and renal-anemia drug.

quick.overview:
Mepitiostane (Thioderon) is an oral steroid the body converts into epitiostanol, combining antiestrogen activity with weak anabolic and androgenic activity. Bodybuilders discuss it for a drier, leaner contest look.

Epitiostanol binds the estrogen receptor as an antagonist and the androgen receptor as an agonist, which is the basis for the less-water, harder-muscle idea. In Japan it has been marketed for breast cancer and for anemia in kidney failure, with a phase III trial against medroxyprogesterone acetate in breast cancer. Animal studies show the intact molecule travels via intestinal lymph, letting part of the dose bypass first-pass liver metabolism. No human study has tested it for appearance.
quick.how: It is an oral prescription drug in Japan. Physique use is based on discussion in bodybuilding circles rather than documented routines.
quick.risks: Wikipedia reports a high rate of virilizing effects in women, such as acne, hirsutism and voice changes. It is prescription-only where sold, and sports authorities prohibit it; urine tests for its metabolites exist.

angle.text: Mepitiostane is discussed for a drier, leaner look: it converts to epitiostanol, which blocks estrogen action and weakly activates androgen receptors. It is used medically in Japan for breast cancer and renal anemia; no appearance studies exist.

epitiostanol.summary: Injectable Japanese antiestrogen steroid (Thiodrol) used for breast cancer, discussed for a drier, harder look and limiting gynecomastia.

quick.overview:
Epitiostanol is a DHT-derived steroid that blocks the estrogen receptor while weakly activating the androgen receptor. Bodybuilders discuss it for a drier, harder look and for limiting gynecomastia.

It has been used in Japan since 1977 as an anticancer drug for breast cancer. In premenopausal women it also suppresses the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis, lowering estrogen. Orally it is broken down extensively in the gut wall and liver, so it has been given by injection; mepitiostane is its oral prodrug. No published trial has tested it for muscle or appearance.
quick.how: Medically it is given by injection in Japan. Physique use is based on discussion rather than documented routines.
quick.risks: Little safety information is published. Its prodrug mepitiostane has a high rate of virilizing effects in women. It is a prescription drug in Japan, and the related methylepitiostanol has appeared as a designer steroid.

angle.text: Epitiostanol is discussed for a drier, harder look: it blocks estrogen action, which bodybuilders associate with less water and less gynecomastia, while weakly activating androgen receptors. It has been studied in breast cancer; the appearance angle has no human data.

furazabol.summary: Oral Japanese anabolic steroid, a close cousin of stanozolol, discussed for lean mass and strength; known in the West from the Ben Johnson doping inquiry.

quick.overview:
Furazabol is an oral anabolic-androgenic steroid marketed in Japan since 1969, structurally nearly identical to stanozolol with a furazan ring in place of its pyrazole ring. Bodybuilders discuss it for lean mass and strength.

It is a 17α-alkylated DHT derivative acting on the androgen receptor, reported to have a relatively high anabolic-to-androgenic ratio. Rat studies reported effects on blood fibrinolysis, and it has been described as lipid-lowering, though author William Llewellyn regards that as a myth. Sources are mostly doping-control and animal studies; in North America it became known through the Dubin Inquiry into Ben Johnson's 1988 case.
quick.how: It was used orally as a medicine in Japan. Physique use is based on discussion rather than documented routines.
quick.risks: As a 17α-alkylated steroid it may carry a risk of liver toxicity. It is Schedule III in the United States and Schedule IV in Canada, and anabolic steroids are prohibited in sport.

angle.text: Furazabol is discussed for lean mass and strength: as an oral stanozolol-like steroid it activates androgen receptors and is reported to have a high anabolic-to-androgenic ratio. Sources are mostly doping and animal studies, with no modern human trials.

oxabolone-cipionate.summary: Obscure long-acting injectable nandrolone-type steroid once marketed in Europe as Steranabol, mentioned for mass gain.

quick.overview:
Oxabolone cipionate is a long-acting injectable ester of oxabolone (4-hydroxy-19-nortestosterone), a nandrolone-type anabolic steroid, marketed in Europe as Steranabol Depo and Steranabol Ritardo. People who follow steroid history mention it for mass gain.

It is a prodrug of oxabolone, given by intramuscular injection, and carried the developmental code FI-5852. Very little has been published: sources do not describe its pharmacology or potency in detail, and no clinical or appearance studies were found.
quick.how: It was marketed as a depot injectable in Europe. Little else is documented about its use.
quick.risks: The only indexed medical report found is a 1995 dermatology paper on mucosal hyperpigmentation attributed to oxabolone. Little else is documented.

angle.text: Oxabolone cipionate is mentioned for mass gain as a nandrolone-type steroid that activates androgen receptors. It was once sold in Europe as Steranabol, and almost nothing about it has been published.

ethylestrenol-maxibolin.summary: Old oral 19-nor anabolic steroid, now veterinary-only, used for lean, low-water mass gains; Wikipedia calls it a very weak muscle-builder.

quick.overview:
Ethylestrenol (Maxibolin, Orabolin) is an oral nandrolone-derived anabolic steroid first described in 1959 and approved in the US in 1964. It was prescribed to promote weight and muscle gain, in catabolic states, and for some anemias and bone conditions; bodybuilders have used it for lean, low-water gains.

It is an androgen receptor agonist with strong progestogenic activity and a high anabolic-to-androgenic ratio, considered a prodrug of norethandrolone, with receptor affinity about 5 percent of testosterone's according to Wikipedia. Wikipedia describes it as a very weak muscle-builder, so it has not been commonly used for physique. It is no longer used in humans and appears to survive only as a veterinary product in a few countries. No appearance trials were found.
quick.how: It was taken orally as a medicine. Physique use has been uncommon and is based on discussion rather than documented routines.
quick.risks: Reported effects include virilization (acne, hirsutism, voice changes) and possible liver damage as a 17α-alkylated steroid. Pregnancy and prostate cancer are contraindications. It is Schedule III in the US and Schedule IV in Canada.

angle.text: Ethylestrenol was used for lean, low-water mass gains: as an oral nandrolone derivative it activates androgen receptors with a high anabolic-to-androgenic ratio. It was studied medically for wasting and anemia, and Wikipedia describes it as a weak muscle-builder.

norethandrolone-nilevar.summary: One of the first oral anabolic steroids (1950s), cited in bodybuilding history as a forerunner for mass; liver injury ended most use.

quick.overview:
Norethandrolone (Nilevar) is an oral 19-nortestosterone steroid synthesized by G. D. Searle in 1953 and introduced as an anabolic steroid in 1956, the first marketed with a favorable separation of anabolic from androgenic effects. It is cited in bodybuilding history as a forerunner of later mass-building steroids.

It was prescribed for muscle wasting, burns, trauma and some aplastic anemias. It is an androgen receptor agonist with strong progestogenic activity, and Wikipedia reports aromatase converts it to ethylestradiol. Human weight-gain data come from mid-century studies of underweight patients, including a 1959 study, and it has not been studied for appearance in modern trials.
quick.how: It was prescribed orally as a medicine in the 1950s and 60s. It is reported to be available today only in France.
quick.risks: Cholestasis, peliosis hepatis and bile canalicular changes were reported in treated patients in 1959 and 1960 papers. It was withdrawn in many countries in the 1980s over liver concerns and is Schedule III in the US.

angle.text: Norethandrolone, an early oral anabolic steroid from the 1950s, promotes nitrogen retention and protein gain, which is why it is cited in bodybuilding history as a forerunner for more muscle and body weight. A 1959 weight-gain study is the main human data point.

mibolerone-cheque-drops.summary: A veterinary oral steroid for dogs that circulates in bodybuilding circles as a very potent pre-workout for strength and aggression.

quick.overview:
Mibolerone is a synthetic androgen that Upjohn sold as Cheque Drops to suppress heat in female dogs; it is not approved for people. In bodybuilding circles it is described as a very potent oral steroid taken for short-term strength and aggression, to push training output and so build more muscle.

It binds the androgen receptor very tightly, and also the progesterone receptor, and its 17-alkyl group makes it orally active. In the lab it is used as a high-affinity androgen receptor ligand in prostate and breast cancer cell studies. The claims about its effects in people come from community reports and extrapolation from its receptor pharmacology; no human trials exist.
quick.how: In bodybuilding circles it is described as an oral pre-workout taken around training. Veterinary use is as an oral drug for dogs.
quick.risks: Animal use is linked to enlarged clitoris, vaginitis and liver changes. Human risks are inferred from other oral steroids, since no human safety data exist. It is controlled in the US, Canada and Brazil and banned in sport.

angle.text: Mibolerone is a potent oral androgen that bodybuilders describe as a strength and drive boost, meant to raise training output and so build more muscle. It is a veterinary drug for dogs; the claims about people come from forum reports.
